title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities?
abstract: arXiv:2611.24330v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We investigate whether a weight edit can alter how a model trades off honoring a commitment against benefiting more people. In a concept-supervised text model, we alter fitted choice weights so that the benefit required to override a formal pledge is larger than for an ordinary promise. Across six independently trained text readers, the edit selects the larger group in both orders on 100% of targeted ordinary conflicts and 83.3% of targeted formal conflicts. It preserves the source model's success rates on smaller conflicts and its factual accuracy. The remaining formal-conflict failures coincide with errors reading a beneficiary number. A separate classifier demonstrates why this distinction matters: reusing a factual answer passes an unconditional choice test but fails to preserve small-gap promises. In a YOLO11n pilot on COCO128, a bias edit increased small-target matches from 3/43 to 9/43, and an equivalent score calibration reprod

translated_title: 权重空间编程能否改变已习得的伦理优先级？
translated_abstract: 我们研究了权重编辑是否能改变模型在“遵守承诺”与“让更多人受益”之间的权衡方式。在一个概念监督的文本模型中，我们修改了拟合得到的选择权重，使得推翻正式誓言所需的收益大于推翻普通承诺所需的收益。在六个独立训练的文本阅读器上，该编辑在两种测试顺序下，对目标普通冲突选择更大群体的成功率为100%，对目标正式冲突的成功率为83.3%。该编辑同时保持了源模型在较小冲突上的成功率以及其事实准确性。剩余的正式冲突失败案例恰好与读取受益人数量时的错误重合。一个独立的分类器演示了为什么这种区分至关重要：复用事实答案可以通过无条件选择测试，却无法保留小差距承诺。在COCO128上的YOLO11n试点实验中，偏置编辑将小目标匹配数从3/43提升至9/43，而等效的分数校准方法重现了……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究表明，通过直接编辑权重空间中的选择权重，可以成功调整模型学习到的伦理优先级——使模型在权衡中更严格地对待正式誓言而非普通承诺，同时不损害其在其他任务上的表现与事实准确性。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that weight-space programming can successfully alter a model's learned ethical priorities, making formal pledges harder to override than ordinary promises while preserving the model's performance on other tasks and its factual accuracy.
